name: Lower Sorbian

ancestors.notes: Descent from Proto-Slavic (West Slavic, Sorbian/Lusatian subgroup).
German adstrate: heavily German-influenced Slavic island in Lower Lusatia; closely related to Upper Sorbian.

notes: Lower Sorbian (Dolnoserbski), West Slavic minority language spoken in Lower Lusatia, Germany. Closely related to Upper Sorbian. Distinct palatal fricatives ś /ɕ/ and ź /ʑ/. More conservative vowel system than Upper Sorbian. Open question: Żygis (2003: 180-181) argues that the ⟨š ž⟩ series is retroflex /ʂ ʐ/ rather than postalveolar, and that the alveolo-palatal affricates have merged with /ɕ ʑ/, which would collapse the ⟨ć⟩ and ⟨ś⟩ distinction kept here.

sources.author: Żygis, Marzena
sources.title: Phonetic and phonological aspects of Slavic sibilant fricatives
sources.notes: Section 2.2 on Lower Sorbian read in full: it argues the ⟨š ž⟩ series is retroflex rather than postalveolar, and reports that the alveolo-palatal affricates have merged with the alveolo-palatal fricatives.

stress.notes: Lower Sorbian (dsb) has categorical initial stress, following the West Slavic pattern shared with Czech. Source: Stone (1993), in The Slavonic Languages; Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Sorbian_language
